lines.text: When I opened my door on my return, Flush threw himself upon me with a most ecstatical agony, and for full ten minutes did not cease jumping and kissing my hands—he thought he had lost me for certain, this time.
lines.note: Flush’s ecstatic welcome home after Elizabeth’s frightening day.

lines.text: Now I will kiss you, dearest: used you to divine that at the very beginning, I have sometimes shortened the visit in order to arrive at the time of taking your hand?
lines.note: Robert’s private confession that he sometimes shortened visits to reach the moment of taking her hand.

lines.text: Write the one line ... do not let me do myself wrong by my anxiety—if I may come, let me!
lines.note: Robert’s tender plea to be allowed to come, all anxiety gathered into one question.

lines.text: I have lost my poor Flush—lost him!
lines.note: The sudden, devastating loss of Flush that coloured their separation.

lines.text: Poor Flush—how sorry I am for you, my Ba!
lines.note: Robert’s immediate sympathy for Elizabeth’s fear and grief over Flush.

lines.text: It seems to me that you and I are at one upon the whole question,—only that I am your Flush, and he is mine.
lines.note: Elizabeth’s private joke turning their whole argument into a love-declaration: ‘you are my Flush, and he is mine.’

lines.text: Only a few words to tell you that Flush is found, and lying on the sofa, with one paw and both ears hanging over the edge of it.
lines.note: Flush recovered at last, lying on the sofa with one paw and both ears over the edge.

lines.text: What do you expect this letter will be about, my own dearest?
lines.note: Robert’s playful, weighty opening as the elopement plan becomes real.

lines.text: Almost everybody is to be away at Richmond, at a picnic, and we shall be free on all sides.
lines.note: Almost everyone away, leaving them free on all sides for the decisive visit.

lines.text: When we drove past that church again, I and my sisters, there was a cloud before my eyes.
lines.note: The cloud before Elizabeth’s eyes as they drove past the church after the wedding.

lines.text: I did hate so, to have to take off the ring!
lines.note: Elizabeth’s bittersweet protest at having to take off the wedding ring.

lines.text: Bless you, my very own, only Ba—my pride, and joy, and utter comfort.
lines.note: Robert’s proud, joyful summary of what Elizabeth has made his life.

lines.text: Your letters to me I take with me, let the ‘ounces’ cry out aloud, ever so.
lines.note: Elizabeth refusing to leave Robert’s letters behind, whatever the ounces cost.

lines.text: I begin to think that none are so bold as the timid, when they are fairly roused.
lines.note: Elizabeth’s final, affectionate reversal: the timid prove boldest when roused.
